page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The hardware configuration features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs from the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor series running at 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity is allocated at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network transfer speed of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput in select algorithms, notably achieving top-tier performance in bzip3 single-threaded decompression at 17.2 GB/sec and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.33 GB/sec. Memory handling is also competent, evidenced by a strong PassMark memory benchmark score of 2876.9 and an average read-only large block memory bandwidth of 66.01 GB/sec. In database-centric evaluations, the instance produced 6.51 million Redis SET operations per second and average static web serving throughput of 8.06 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff stems from the limited aggregate core count. Multi-core performance metrics, such as PassMark overall CPU score (2191.41) and multi-core stress-ng tests, rank in the lower percentiles relative to broader cloud hardware. Heavy computational workloads such as medium-tier 7B LLM inference execute poorly at 4.77 tokens per second. However, for entry-level deployments requiring low-latency NVMe temporary scratch storage and solid single-thread execution, the hardware profile delivers balanced resource efficiency without requiring overprovisioned multi-socket compute capacity.

Given the combination of local NVMe storage, dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores, and balanced memory, the instance functions effectively for caching layers, lightweight database nodes, local data decompression tasks, and edge web-serving applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 vCPUs clocked at 3.3 GHz, 8.0 GB of memory, and 118 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic testing highlights strong single-threaded performance in compression routines, including top-tier bzip3 decompression and solid memory benchmarks, alongside steady throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving. While overall multi-core computational throughput is constrained by the two-core layout, the integration of local high-speed NVMe storage paired with dedicated Arm cores provides balanced resource utility for distributed caches, web serving, and database workloads requiring fast temporary storage.
